clue.text: Bigwig with big backing from primate

indicators.note: backing means the two words before it are read together from right to left

parts.note: a nob is a bigwig, a person of high standing
taken as written

explanation.surface: An important person gets generous support from an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns both pieces round together; the ape is the puzzle's theme word, the surname shared by several clues marked '1s'.
explanation.definitionFit: The gibbon is a small long-armed ape, so it is an example of a primate.

clue.text: All turn — that's demanded out of spite

indicators.note: letters demanded out are forced from their places, so the fodder is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Everyone takes a turn only because it is required, grudgingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demanded out' shuffles ALL, TURN and IE (from 'that's') into the two-word answer; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill nature is a malicious disposition, a near synonym for spite or malevolence.

clue.text: I won't allow you to flag

definitions.meaning: the speaker forbids things, so is one who bans
a flag is a long cloth standard carried in procession

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the answer as BAN + -NER, someone who bans.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a flag on a pole, and whimsically also a person who forbids.

clue.text: Pasta with Benedictine in the realm of folly

parts.note: noodles are a kind of pasta
Dom is the title given to a Benedictine monk

explanation.surface: A monk sits down to spaghetti in a foolish world.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is a fool, and the suffix -dom makes a realm, so the word means the domain of fools.

clue.text: The fisherman's whim

definitions.meaning: an angler's bait, the larva of a fly put on the hook
an old sense meaning a fanciful notion or caprice

explanation.definitionFit: A grub used as angling bait, and in older English a crotchety fancy or whim.

clue.text: Two generations could be free

parts.note: a mother is one generation
a son is the next generation

explanation.surface: A family spanning two generations might be liberated.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to a freemason: a mason could be 'free'.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the brotherhood are Freemasons, so a builder in stone could be called free.

clue.text: 1s putting a smile on a fish

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Apes grin at a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: '1s' refers to 1 across: the woodcarver Grinling Gibbons is one of the theme's Gibbonses.
explanation.definitionFit: Grinling Gibbons was the celebrated seventeenth-century woodcarver bearing that surname.

clue.text: POW camp with prisoners' regulator?

definitions.meaning: a German camp for captured officers in wartime
a camp is the thing that controls inmates, the question mark admitting the stretch

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense also plays on OF LAG, as if the camp belonged to the convicts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oflag (Offizierslager) was a German prison camp for officers captured in war.

clue.text: The country round follows alternative 1s

indicators.note: follows puts the country-and-round pieces after the alternative

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
land is a word for a country
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A nation circles behind other apes.
explanation.walkthrough: '1s' again means a Gibbons: Orlando Gibbons the Jacobean composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando Gibbons was an English composer of the early seventeenth century.

clue.text: Heal portico that's collapsed: is this correctly pronounced?

indicators.note: something collapsed has fallen into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: After repairing a fallen porch, someone asks whether the word is said right.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthoepy is the study of correct pronunciation, so the adjective means pronounced properly.

clue.text: Winter sports association for 51 bucks, maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests a possible rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snow club charges fifty-one dollars a head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' shuffles LI with BUCKS; 'bucks' looks like money but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A club for skiers is a society organised around a winter sport.

clue.text: Drink in Germany — please get the right answer

parts.note: bitte is German for please, the language flagged by 'in Germany'
from the phrase 'the answer's a lemon', meaning the answer is no

explanation.surface: In Germany someone begs to be given the correct solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Germany' says the word for please is German.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbonated soft drink flavoured with lemon and quinine.

clue.text: Ignis fatuus for back-packers?

parts.note: a will-o'-the-wisp is a wandering glow over marshes; hikers carrying little are said to journey with a small load

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means journeying with little luggage, and literally a moving glow such as marsh gas.

clue.text: Address to Manx cat by 8 across 1s, maybe

parts.note: O is the vocative used when addressing someone

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: A greeting to a tailless cat from Orlando Gibbons.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'a work by Orlando Gibbons, for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical composition is numbered as a work, so a piece by a composer is one example.

clue.text: A barrier against Tyneside must be unbreakable

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water
anti means against
NE, the North East of England, where Tyneside lies

explanation.surface: A dam to keep out Newcastle must be built strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamantine means as hard as adamant, so impossible to break.

clue.text: Beasts and bird in battle

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: Mons is a First World War battle in Belgium
a goose is a bird

explanation.surface: Animals and a bird are caught up in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Mongooses are small carnivorous mammals, plural animals or beasts.

clue.text: Heath makes himself known about scheme that wasn't there at first

indicators.note: about means the introduction goes round the next piece

parts.note: Edward (Ted) Heath introducing himself says 'I'm Ted'
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister introduces himself to unveil a novel plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath was a British Prime Minister in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implanted was put in later, so it was not present originally.

clue.text: Two churches on song: a worm will follow

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
RC is Roman Catholic
an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: Two congregations sing, then a worm crawls after them.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a larval stage of a parasitic fluke, from which the adult worm later develops.

clue.text: Before there's an upheaval, get a better job

parts.note: pre- means before
a ferment is a state of agitation or upheaval

explanation.surface: Ahead of a shake-up, someone lands a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Preferment is promotion to a higher office or position.

clue.text: Precious little 12 for others

parts.note: op. is the short form of the work in 12 across
al. abbreviates Latin alii, others, as in et al.

explanation.surface: A treasured short piece of music is meant for other people.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stands for a precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The opal is a precious gemstone, standing in for the adjective here.

clue.text: A girl to confess being inside it

indicators.note: being inside puts the confession within the next piece

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is a crossword sense of 'it'
to tell is to confess

explanation.surface: A girl owns up to being in on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Stella Gibbons wrote the novel at 20 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella is a girl's name, here also the novelist Stella Gibbons.

clue.text: Change from cad with clot and from 19 1s' 12

indicators.note: change says the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddled sentence about swapping a cad for a clot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'Stella Gibbons' work': the comic novel of 1932.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1932 comic novel is the best-known book by the writer Stella Gibbons.

clue.text: Grey cover containing 6

indicators.note: containing places one piece within the other

parts.note: a lid is a cover
IV is 6 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A grey lid holds six items.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid can mean a leaden blue-grey colour, as of a bruise.

clue.text: Matched and dispatched?

definitions.meaning: paired up, as animals or partners are
finished off, as a king is in chess

explanation.walkthrough: Echoes 'hatched, matched and dispatched', a jokey name for births, marriages and deaths notices.
explanation.definitionFit: Mated means paired, and in chess the king checkmated is finished.

clue.text: Young creature for hire, always to be taken in

indicators.note: the word for always is enclosed in the word for hire

parts.note: to let is to hire out
ever means always

explanation.surface: A youngster is offered for rent forever.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a young hare in its first year.

clue.text: Nobel prizewinner could be lost in a tabloid

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled letters inside the paper

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prize winner's name might go missing in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' looks like the subject of 'could be lost', but it is the fodder; John Sulston was the 2002 laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: John Sulston shared the 2002 Nobel Prize in medicine for work on cell development.

clue.text: Waged war determinedly to show 1

indicators.note: to show means the letters are on display within the words

explanation.surface: Someone fought fiercely to make their mark.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' is 1 across: Edward Gibbon, historian of the Roman Empire's decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Gibbon wrote The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Literary hero's drunk

definitions.meaning: Tristram, the hero of Laurence Sterne's novel
something drunk, a beer mixed with lemonade

explanation.definitionFit: Tristram is Sterne's narrator, and the drink is beer diluted with lemonade.
